seo.title: BMW: generative AI as a brand creative engine - Mega Me, projected art, iX3 spot (2023-2026)
seo.meta_description: BMW industrializes generative AI in brand creative: Mega Me experience (15,000+ visitors), AI-generated art on the 8 Series, an iX3 spot fully generated by AI.
seo.resume_citable: BMW uses generative AI as a brand creative engine: the Mega Me experience at BMW Welt drew more than 15,000 visitors in 2023, a campaign projected art generated by a model trained on 50,000 paintings, and a 30-second iX3 spot was fully generated by AI in 2026.

faq.q: How does BMW use generative AI in marketing?
faq.a: For brand experiences and campaigns: the Mega Me installation at BMW Welt, AI-generated art projected onto its vehicles, and an iX3 spot fully generated by AI.
More than 15,000 visitors for Mega Me in the first half of 2023, an art model trained on more than 50,000 paintings, and an iX3 spot in which every frame was generated by AI.

pattern: advertising and experiential creation with generative AI
objectif_business: Use generative AI as a brand creative engine: create experiences and campaigns that get people talking, generate earned media, and position BMW on the innovation front, while testing when AI creation works and when it does not.
description: BMW has industrialized generative AI in its brand creative across several formats. At BMW Welt in Munich, the Mega Me experience (January to September 2023) let visitors take a selfie and then see themselves animated in real time on a 42-square-meter 3D LED screen, at the wheel of the BMW i Vision Dee, via Reface's face-swap technology with the agency Elastique. On another campaign, a model trained on more than 50,000 paintings generated works projected onto the BMW 8 Series Gran Coupe, with Goodby, Silverstein and Partners. More recently, BMW produced a 30-second spot for the iX3 fully generated by AI, with no camera or crew, presented by the brand as a test of the process as much as of the result.

resultats.metrique: Visitors who tried the Mega Me experience (January to May 2023)
Training corpus of the art model, 900 years of history (8 Series)
iX3 spot fully generated by AI

niveau_preuve.justification: Several distinct brand formats, dated and quantified (15,000 visitors, corpus of 50,000 paintings), documented by the established marketing press and a case study from the technical provider; no financial metric isolating the commercial impact, hence level C.

stack_technique.detail: Face-swap and real-time rendering technology for the Mega Me experience: the visitor's selfie is converted into anonymized vectors then animated on the 3D screen.
Art model trained on more than 50,000 paintings for the 8 Series campaign and video generation for the iX3 spot; the sources do not name the exact models.
Creative agency for the Mega Me experience at BMW Welt.
Agency for the AI-generated art campaign projected onto the BMW 8 Series Gran Coupe.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Per campaign or per event activation; real-time rendering on the visitor experience side (Mega Me).
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: BMW's brand and marketing teams, with creative agencies (Elastique., Goodby Silverstein) and a technical provider (Reface) for the AI part.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The creative input: the visitor's selfie for Mega Me, the reference corpus of works for the generated art, the brief and references for the AI spot. Without art direction and continuity control, the generated output drifts.

etapes.detail: BMW and the agency define the concept and the references (works, style, message).
The generative model is trained or tuned on the reference corpus (for example 50,000 paintings).
The AI produces the image, video, or real-time animation (Mega Me face-swap, projected art, iX3 spot).
The teams validate continuity and rendering, then distribute as an installation, projection, or spot.

prerequis_data: possible user input (photo) with biometric consent
prerequis_orga: quality control on continuity and brand compliance
stack_possible: face-swap / vision for the experiential part
replication.premiere_etape: Choose an activation with high earned-media potential and prototype the generated rendering before exposing it to the public.

playbook.action: Choose the activation (event, campaign) and frame the concept with the agency; check the legal framework, in particular rights and biometric data if a selfie is involved.
playbook.livrable: Creative brief and legal analysis validated.

playbook.action: Prototype the generated rendering: tune or train the model on the reference corpus (works, brand assets).
playbook.livrable: Proof of concept validated by art direction.

playbook.action: Produce the final asset and control continuity and brand compliance frame by frame.
playbook.livrable: Asset ready to distribute (installation, projection, or spot).

playbook.action: Deploy the activation and measure participation, press coverage, and engagement.
playbook.livrable: Activation assessment: visitors, earned media, lessons.

replication.equipe: 1 art director / brand lead + 1 creative agency + 1 AI technical provider (rendering, face-swap, generation).

statut_vivant.note: BMW continues to use generative AI in brand creative, through the iX3 spot fully generated by AI presented in April 2026; the Mega Me experience ran from January to late September 2023.

transposable_ue.note: Part of the setup originated in the EU (BMW Welt, Munich). The point of attention concerns the processing of the selfie and the face (sensitive biometric data under GDPR): in the Mega Me case, the faces were converted into anonymized vectors.
